text: RTEL1, a helicase promoting t-loop unwinding and suppressing telomere fragility, is recruited to telomeres by the shelterin protein TRF2 during S phase, preventing catastrophic t-loop processing by structure-specific nucleases. This interaction requires a metal-coordinating C4C4 motif in RTEL1; it is disrupted by the Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome (HHS) mutation RTEL1(R1264H). A TRF2(I124D) substitution in the TRFH domain abolishes RTEL1 binding and phenocopies RTEL1(R1264H), producing aberrant t-loop excision, telomere length heterogeneity, and loss of the telomere as a circle. These findings show TRF2 recruits RTEL1 to disassemble t-loops at telomeres in S phase, maintaining vertebrate telomere integrity.
